name: Hakupha
overview: Hakupha was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role was connected to the religious duties associated with the temple, emphasizing his participation in the worship life of Israel. Scripture mentions him specifically in the context of the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Hakupha means 'crooked,' which is noted as a proper name. There is no indication that this name was given by God, but it identifies him uniquely among the Levites mentioned in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Hakupha is identified as a descendant of Levi, establishing his tribal lineage. Beyond this, Scripture does not record any further family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Hakupha's significance lies in his role as a temple servant from the tribe of Levi, highlighting the restoration of worship and temple service after the exile. His mention in Ezra 2:51 underscores the faithfulness of the Levites who returned to Jerusalem and resumed their sacred duties, contributing to the reestablishment of God's covenant community.
